Thesis workspace verification
Audit date: 2026-10-27

Scope
The generic Quarto editor shell, thesis.js, thesis-compiler.js, the compiler
worker and static runtime assets, and the owner-restricted thesisWorkspace
Firebase callable. The rendered artifact is /tools/thesis.html. Shared browser
authentication was reused, not migrated. Private project files are stored in
Firebase and are not included in the published editor assets.

Boundaries checked
The server authorizes the designated account on every request. It checks the
provider, active session, production origin, and consumed App Check token.
Record validation, file/project byte limits, owner/address/global quotas,
revision comparisons, five prior saves, and deletion tombstones run on the
server. Browser users cannot read or write the private database branch directly.
The live username binding and runtime App Check verifier role were checked.

The browser displays source and compiler logs as text. Imports have schema and
byte limits. Sign-out clears text and revisions, terminates compilation,
revokes download URLs, and invalidates late asynchronous responses. Compilation
uses a temporary worker with exact self-hosted asset paths, bounded fetch,
fixed binary synchronous reads, a two-minute watchdog, and bounded PDF/log
results. Unknown TeX filenames never become network requests. Report-only CSP
is not an enforced boundary and has no reporting endpoint.

Corrections and review
Claude reviewed the generic code in three rounds and returned APPROVE with no
blocking findings in the third round. The actual reviewer model identifier was
not exposed. Private thesis text and personal research motivation were excluded.
Corrections include cold-instance save proposals, binary request-mode/size
checks, clear session errors, a request envelope that accepts dense LaTeX,
deletion cleanup, and bounded download URLs. A subsequent missing-compiler
fallback was checked with browser regressions. Model review does not replace
the deterministic checks below.

Validation completed
122 backend tests passed, including parser-advisory regressions, owner/session
checks, quotas, malformed/oversized text, revision conflicts, deletion, bounded
history, and a maximum-size project with JSON-escaped LaTeX characters.
Two actual database emulator tests passed, covering all direct-browser denials
and real Admin SDK cold save, conflict, and tombstone behavior.
22 served-page browser checks passed in Chromium and Firefox. They include
real multi-file PDF output, the full initial chapter structure, literal hostile
source, conflicts, restore, late responses, cancellation, watchdog timeout,
sign-out during compilation, URL cleanup, missing compiler assets, and unknown
TeX file probes. Browser sign-in was mocked with synthetic content in these
tests. Real owner-browser login against production remains to be exercised.

Targeted Quarto rendering, JavaScript syntax checks, scoped dangerous-API scans,
private-plan sentinel checks, and source/render parity passed. The generic
Quarto helper inherits its existing baseline. The new vendor exception records
seven XMLHttpRequest constructions with worker-only synchronous reads; no
eval, Function constructor, HTML sink, importScripts, or WebSocket appeared in
the vendor scan. The exception has a 2026-10-27 review date and a 2026-11-17
reassessment deadline, or earlier on any relevant change.

Versions and limitations
Quarto 1.10.18. Existing Firebase browser compat SDK 10.12.0, Admin 13.10.0,
Functions 7.3.2, and deployed Node.js 22. Local backend checks ran with Node
25.9.0. Playwright 1.62.1 and rules-unit-testing 5.0.2. Emulator 4.11.2 used a
checksum-verified temporary Temurin JRE 21.0.13, not a system Java installation.

Compatible transitive patches pin body-parser 2.4.0 and qs 6.17.0. The subsequent
exact-lockfile npm audit has no high/critical findings and eight moderate
findings in the existing optional Google dependency chain, stemming from uuid
buffer APIs. The new workspace does not use those APIs. Broader SDK migration
remains separate maintenance work. The old WebAssembly interpreter is outside
npm audit coverage. Its pinned bytes and worker limits do not establish absence
of unknown vulnerabilities. See NOTICE.txt and checksums.json for provenance,
original licenses, upstream source, and the missing reproducible-build attestation.

PDF compilation targets main.tex with a fixed package set and a 2020 LaTeX
format. Full Quarto rendering, Biber, binary figures, and the final university
submission template are not included in this initial workspace. Project export
is a portable JSON backup; individual text files can be downloaded separately.
Stored source is not end-to-end encrypted. Administrators and the storage
provider can administer it. Live deletion removes the project and its saved
revisions; provider backups have a separate retention policy.
